findings.summary: The test includes a check that cannot start, so verification will also fail and the job will not land. Yet the plan's 'fails without the behavior' says a verdict changed by the baseline would stop the job from landing.
findings.evidence: The verifier runs every configured check in order and stops at the first failure (routing.rs:120 run_local). `/nonexistent/athena-baseline-check` cannot start in the verify snapshot either, so the candidate verdict is a fail whether or not a baseline exists. The landing assertion described in 'Fails without the behavior' cannot be made in this test. Fix: In this test, assert the expected rejection, with the verification naming only the nonexistent check as failing. Put the check that a check failing on the base does not change the verdict (the job lands) in the criterion-2 test, which uses only the grep check that passes on the candidate.

findings.summary: No demonstration covers the case where the whole baseline cannot run, for example when the snapshot or the environment cannot be built.
findings.evidence: The reading assumes 'If the baseline cannot run at all, the job proceeds and the record says so.' The unit tests in checks.rs cover only `baseline_runs` for each check. The wrapper in run.rs that turns a snapshot or environment Err into a record with a note is not tested. Fix: Factor out the conversion from Err to a note-only Baseline as a small pure function and unit-test it. Or add a run.rs unit test that calls take_baseline with a base commit that does not exist, and asserts an empty-checks record with a note and no error.
findings.location: Steps 4 and Risks: take_baseline mapping any error to an empty-checks record

findings.summary: Both additions outside the listed deliverables are needed, and the plan states why.
findings.evidence: store.rs:216-230: `job_of` matches the kinds it knows and returns None for everything else, so `JobRecords` would never hold a baseline. docs/records.md lists the per-job files. Fix: No change needed. Keep the stated reasons in the producer's report.

summary: I read the code and found the plan sound, so I accept it. The places it names exist and work as it assumes. `produce_and_verify` (run.rs:1215) works out `seq` and then makes the producer's snapshot with `SnapshotRepo::Base` before the producer loop, so a baseline taken just after `seq` is set comes from the base and runs before the producer. `run_check` (checks.rs:143) already turns a command that cannot start into a failed `CheckRun` with a "could not start" note. It also kills a check at its deadline with a note, and it redacts the output tail and caps it at `TAIL_BYTES` (4096). The nested-run branch (run.rs:1592) sets the precedent for a record that holds only a note. The fixture's README starts as "# Demo" and the fake producer adds "Hello, reader.", so the `grep -q Hello README.md` check fails on the base and passes on the candidate. Routing does not skip a custom check that has no `skip_when_only`. The plan leaves verify.rs and routing.rs alone. Athena's two scope findings (store.rs and docs/records.md) are justified: `store::job_of` ends in `_ => None`, so without the store.rs change the baseline record would not be read back as part of the job. The remaining issues are minor. The criterion-3 lifecycle test cannot also show the job landing. The case where the whole baseline cannot run has no demonstration.
